newsitem.title: USA: Hollinger Int'l to sell $400 mln in junk bonds.
newsitem.headline: Hollinger Int'l to sell $400 mln in junk bonds.

text.p: Hollinger International Inc, an international newspaper publishing company, plans to raise $400 million in a public offering of high-yield bonds in the U.S. over the next several weeks, a company official said.
Proceeds from the offering will be used to pay down bank debt in connection with recent acquisitions, said the official who asked not to be named.
The deal is the first takedown from a $1.3 billion shelf registration filed last year, he said.
Last year, Hollinger acquired the remaining 36 percent interest in the Daily Telegraph and Sunday Telegraph that it did not previously own for $572 million.
The company, together with Hollinger Inc, also recently acquired a majority interest in Southam Inc, a Canadian newpaper and magazine publisher.
Hollinger Inc based in Vancouver, B.C., is the controlling shareholder of Hollinger International.
The upcoming offering will consist of $200 million of senior notes due 2005 and $200 million of senior subordinated notes 2007.
Merrill Lynch & Co has been chosen as the lead underwriter.
The debt will by issued by Hollinger International Publishing Inc, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hollinger International, he said.
The company already has $250 million in 9 1/4 percent guaranteed senior subordinated notes due 2006 outstanding which are rated B1/BB-minus
